messages.subject: batch effect vs covariates
parts:
Hi,

Maybe this is a silly question. I see that methylkit has different options to account for the effect of cofactors. The batch effect function will use the principal components of the percent methylation and check for associations, whereas the covariates will compare a full model versus a reduced model (with and without the covariate).
Not being mathematician nor statistician i am wondering what is the difference between the two methods, if any, and why is it then possible to check for batch effect with the covariates method. Thanks in advance for clarification and sorry for the naive quiestion.

Regards,
Aziza

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: batch effect vs covariates
parts: The short answer is that if you know the batches you can use them as covariates in your models. Another way to do this is that you can try to remove batch effect from the data. Maybe if you see that your batches do not associate with PCs, you may decide to ignore them.
